name: Subdued

tenures.source: promotions/lcw-ltd/archive/ltd-wrestlers.html
the federation's own roleplay board and its served show documents (promotions/lcw-mercury/)

caption: A technician who came up out of LCW's developmental federation and, in the roleplay half's own words, had yet to establish himself there — lost a Progressive title eliminator to Humpy in LTD's own last Progression show before it went independent.

name: Venom

tenures.source: the federation's own served show documents (promotions/lcw-ltd/)
tenures.note: Interfered in the New Blood Rising tournament final on Yobbo's behalf, then took the LTD Championship from him at an uncaptured show before Winter's Wrath. Retained the title against Myrddin at Winter's Wrath (11 January 2002) — the surviving record does not capture when or how he lost it back.

caption: LTD's own Commissioner, who took the LTD Championship off Bob Yobbo Junior between shows and defended it against Myrddin at Winter's Wrath.

identity.note: Shares the ring name Venom with wrestlers in four unrelated federations (GIWF, CSWA, OWW, and Venom Alexander of GW); no document names any of them together, and a shared one-word ring name across unrelated feds is never a merge on its own.

name: Poltergeist

tenures.source: the federation's own served show documents (promotions/lcw-ltd/)
tenures.note: Lost a Falls Count Anywhere match to Black Wolf at Winter's Wrath (11 January 2002) in a hardcore brawl through the arena's own backstage area. Won a Progressive title eliminator against Huffman at the 19 March 2002 Progression show, then was chased off by HaVoC before Humpy made the save.

caption: Carried a bat he called "The Disturber" to the ring, and traded a bloody hardcore war with Black Wolf up and down LTD's own halls at Winter's Wrath.

identity.note: Shares the ring name Poltergeist with a CCW Cyberspace wrestler active 2005, three years after LTD's own run ends; no document names both, and a shared name across unrelated feds is never a merge on its own.

name: Black Wolf

tenures.source: the federation's own served show documents (promotions/lcw-ltd/)
tenures.note: Defeated Poltergeist in a Falls Count Anywhere match at Winter's Wrath (11 January 2002). Billed to team with Barabbas in the LTD Tag Team Tournament.

caption: Beat Poltergeist in a bloody Falls Count Anywhere brawl at Winter's Wrath that ended with both men driven through a pile of chairs.

name: Damien Diablo

tenures.source: the federation's own served show documents (promotions/lcw-ltd/)
tenures.note: Lost a Progressive title challenge to champion Headbuster at Winter's Wrath (11 January 2002) after Barabbas, blinded by Headbuster's own fire-breath, mistakenly chokeslammed him instead. Billed for LTD's own New Blood Rising tournament, where a match-ending injury against Venom put him in the hospital.

caption: Came back from injury to challenge for the LTD Progressive Championship at Winter's Wrath, walked to the ring with Kittie Brackish and a wall of fire.

name: Kittie Brackish

tenures.source: the federation's own served show documents (promotions/lcw-ltd/)
tenures.note: Accompanied Damien Diablo to the ring for his Progressive title challenge at Winter's Wrath (11 January 2002).

caption: Walked Damien Diablo to the ring at Winter's Wrath as his own arm went up in flame.

name: Jason Stevens

tenures.source: the federation's own served show documents (promotions/lcw-ltd/)
tenures.note: Lost to Scott Royal in the first round of the New Blood Rising tournament (17 November 2001) on a rolled-up tights assist. Interfered in Barabbas's own #1 contendership match against Royal at Winter's Wrath, drawing the disqualification, and helped beat down Matt Henstock in that same show's Presidential match.

caption: Billed as "The Icon," lost the LTD tournament's own sleeper of the night to Scott Royal, and later cost Barabbas a Progressive title shot by running in at Winter's Wrath.

name: Scott Royal

tenures.source: the federation's own served show documents (promotions/lcw-ltd/)
tenures.note: Beat Jason Stevens and lost to Bob Yobbo Jr. across the New Blood Rising tournament (17 November 2001). Lost a #1 contendership to Barabbas at Winter's Wrath, but by 19 March 2002 held the LTD Progressive Championship (won off Headbuster at an uncaptured show) and defended a #1 contender's match against Headbuster by DQ, clocking him with the belt itself.

caption: Reached the New Blood Rising final four on a rolled-up tights assist, and by March 2002 was walking around with the LTD Progressive Championship he'd taken off Headbuster.

identity.note: A pre-split lcw wrestler named Scott Royal debuted once on the Thursday Tempest card of 9 August 2001, before LTD's own 31 October 2001 founding; no document in this corpus's own reading confirms the two are the same performer, so the rows are kept apart. Also shares the name with an unrelated EWO wrestler already flagged distinct on that row.

name: Inferno Kid

tenures.source: the federation's own served show documents (promotions/lcw-ltd/)
tenures.note: Billed against Bob Yobbo Jr. for a title rematch as of LTD's own December 2001 front page; lost the No-DQ match itself at Winter's Wrath (11 January 2002) after Venom's interference backfired.

caption: Lost a No-DQ #1 contender's rematch to Bob Yobbo Junior at Winter's Wrath after Venom slipped him a foreign object that never connected.

identity.note: A pre-split lcw wrestler named Inferno Kid was mentioned once, as a hypothetical future pairing with Dexter Riot, in December 2001 — around LTD's own founding; no document in this corpus's own reading confirms the two are the same performer, so the rows are kept apart.

name: Willie Style

tenures.source: the federation's own served show documents (promotions/lcw-ltd/)
tenures.note: Teamed with Michael Djin as newcomers, losing the LTD Tag Tournament play-in match to Kensuke Suzahara and Jin Akujin at Winter's Wrath (11 January 2002).

caption: Billed "The Loose Cannon," lost a tag play-in at Winter's Wrath to Street Samurai after his own partner's distraction ran out.

name: Michael Djin

tenures.source: the federation's own served show documents (promotions/lcw-ltd/)
tenures.note: Teamed with Willie Style as newcomers, losing the LTD Tag Tournament play-in match to Kensuke Suzahara and Jin Akujin at Winter's Wrath (11 January 2002).

caption: Billed "The Crimson Lord," flipped off the crowd on his way to a tag play-in loss at Winter's Wrath.

name: Kensuke Suzahara

tenures.source: the federation's own served show documents (promotions/lcw-ltd/)
tenures.note: Debuted at Winter's Wrath (11 January 2002), teaming with Jin Akujin as Street Samurai to beat Willie Style and Michael Djin in the LTD Tag Tournament play-in. Billed for a tag semifinal against Bob Yobbo Jr. and Headbuster on the 1 February 2002 card, results uncaptured.

caption: Won LTD's own tag tournament play-in as half of Street Samurai at Winter's Wrath, writing "LCW" on his own bloodied stomach mid-match.

identity.note: Shares the exact ring name Kensuke Suzahara with wrestlers already registered in PURE and CCW Cyberspace, the latter itself already flagged as a coincidence worth a second look against PURE's own row. No document connects any of the three; kept distinct pending a future pass with more context on either wing.

name: Brutakis

tenures.source: the federation's own served show documents (promotions/lcw-ltd/)
tenures.note: Teamed with Bones as HaVoC to win a tag tables match against Humpy and Baine at Winter's Wrath (11 January 2002), then again — with Maxx Vain added, billed Ruthless Inc. — lost the LTD Championship/Tag Team title six-man to Global Warning on 19 March 2002.

caption: Half of HaVoC (later billed Ruthless Inc.), a 7'2" powerhouse who military-pressed Baine like a set of dumbbells at Winter's Wrath; Ruthless Inc. held the LTD Tag Team Championship before losing it to Global Warning on 19 March 2002.

name: Bones

tenures.source: the federation's own served show documents (promotions/lcw-ltd/)
tenures.note: Teamed with Brutakis as HaVoC to win a tag tables match against Humpy and Baine at Winter's Wrath (11 January 2002), then again — with Maxx Vain added, billed Ruthless Inc. — lost the LTD Championship/Tag Team title six-man to Global Warning on 19 March 2002.

caption: Half of HaVoC (later billed Ruthless Inc.), and the one who insisted the pair were never TwiZtiD; Ruthless Inc. held the LTD Tag Team Championship before losing it to Global Warning on 19 March 2002.

name: Cotton

tenures.source: the federation's own served show documents (promotions/lcw-ltd/)
tenures.note: Accompanied HaVoC/Ruthless Inc. to the ring across Winter's Wrath and the 19 March 2002 Progression show, and traded blows with Baine at the latter.

caption: HaVoC's own valet, billed "Cotton Candy" in the ring gear, slapped and threatened around the ring on their behalf.

name: Humpy

tenures.source: the federation's own served show documents (promotions/lcw-ltd/)
tenures.note: Teamed with Baine as Grevious Bodily Harm, losing a tag tables match to HaVoC at Winter's Wrath (11 January 2002). By March 2002 fought as a singles wrestler, beating Subdued for a Progressive title shot and running off HaVoC's attack on his own former rival Poltergeist.

caption: A 7-foot-plus monster billed "Death By Humpy," half of the short-lived Grevious Bodily Harm before turning on his own former partner's attackers.

name: Baine

tenures.role: wrestler — Grevious Bodily Harm; Global Warning
tenures.source: the federation's own served show documents (promotions/lcw-ltd/)
tenures.note: Teamed with Humpy as Grevious Bodily Harm, losing a tag tables match to HaVoC at Winter's Wrath. By 19 March 2002 teamed with Myrddin and Parker Louis as Global Warning, winning the LTD Tag Team Championship (with Parker Louis) in the same six-man that kept Myrddin's LTD Championship.

caption: Half of Grevious Bodily Harm, then Global Warning, and by 19 March 2002 co-holder of the LTD Tag Team Championship.

name: Parker Louis

tenures.source: the federation's own served show documents (promotions/lcw-ltd/)
tenures.note: Teamed with Myrddin and Baine as Global Warning at the 19 March 2002 Progression show, winning the LTD Tag Team Championship alongside Baine in the same six-man that kept Myrddin's LTD Championship.

caption: Billed "Neon," the third member of Global Warning, who tagged in against Maxx Vain in a shoot-style stance at the 19 March 2002 Progression show.

identity.note: Shares the decorated ring name "Neon" Parker Louis exactly with a CCW Cyberspace wrestler active in 2005, three years after the held record's run ends. No document connects the two; kept distinct pending a future pass with more context on either wing.

name: Maxx Vain

tenures.source: the federation's own served show documents (promotions/lcw-ltd/)
tenures.note: Wrestled alongside Bones and Brutakis, billed Ruthless Inc., losing the LTD Championship/Tag Team title six-man to Global Warning on 19 March 2002.

caption: A technical wrestler added to HaVoC (billed Ruthless Inc.) by 19 March 2002, when the LTD Championship and Tag Team titles both rode on his own match.

name: Tommy Steele

tenures.source: the federation's own served show documents (promotions/lcw-ltd/)
tenures.note: Beat Viper in a Contract Match opening the 19 March 2002 Progression show. Billed for the LTD Gauntlet at the never-captured Genesis supercard.

caption: Billed "the war train," opened the 19 March 2002 Progression show with a reverse-stunner off the second rope that ended Viper's night.

name: Viper

tenures.source: the federation's own served show documents (promotions/lcw-ltd/)
tenures.note: Lost a Contract Match to Tommy Steele on the 19 March 2002 Progression show, LTD's own last show under that name.

caption: Lost his own LTD debut, a Contract Match against Tommy Steele, on 19 March 2002.

identity.note: Shares the ring name Viper with wrestlers in five unrelated federations (WWA, SCW Survival, XCWF, NGW, LOW); no document names any of them together, and a shared one-word ring name across unrelated feds is never a merge on its own.

name: Sloan Malice

tenures.source: the federation's own served show documents (promotions/lcw-ltd/)
tenures.note: Challenged Barabbas for the LTD Lethal Championship in a Hardcore Steel Cage match at the 19 March 2002 Progression show, billed as having "a falling out with management in Mercury."

caption: Attacked LTD's own Lethal Champion Barabbas with a 2x4 inside a Hardcore Steel Cage on 19 March 2002 and lost anyway.

identity.note: Shares part of a name with sloan-lcw-mercury, a Mercury wrestler; the held record's line billing Sloan Malice as having "a falling out with management in Mercury" is suggestive but names no shared match, date, or detail confirming the two are the same performer, so the rows are kept apart pending stronger evidence.

name: Matt Henstock

tenures.source: the federation's own served show documents (promotions/lcw-ltd/)
tenures.note: Returned at Winter's Wrath (11 January 2002) to contest Paxton's own hold on the LTD Presidency in a street fight, losing after Venom, Inferno Kid, Jason Stevens, Scott Royal and HaVoC all interfered on Paxton's behalf. Returned again on 19 March 2002, signed by new owner Blaze McCoy for an in-ring comeback, and booked into the never-captured Genesis supercard's own Gauntlet match.

caption: LTD's own founding President, billed "the Big Shot" and "the King of Old School," who returned from a leave of absence to challenge Jacob Paxton for the office and lost.

name: Dr. Jacob Paxton

tenures.source: the federation's own served show documents (promotions/lcw-ltd/)
tenures.note: Won a street-fight defense of the LTD Presidency against Matt Henstock at Winter's Wrath (11 January 2002) via heavy interference from Venom, Inferno Kid, Jason Stevens, Scott Royal and HaVoC. Also billed "Masked Man" on the 1 February 2002 card, a disguise he admitted to on-air at the 19 March 2002 Progression show, the same night new owner Blaze McCoy stripped him of sole authority over the promotion.

caption: LTD's own President, a Steel City Committee alumnus who fixed his own tag-tournament lottery and beat Matt Henstock for the office with five other wrestlers' help.

name: Chad Madden

tenures.source: the federation's own served show documents (promotions/lcw-ltd/)
tenures.note: Called LTD's own New Blood Rising recap, Winter's Wrath, and the 19 March 2002 Progression show, siding openly with the fed's own heels throughout.

caption: LTD's own main commentator, self-billed "Disciple of Dialogue," who called Winter's Wrath and the 19 March 2002 Progression show alongside a rotating cast of co-hosts.

name: Mike Boom

tenures.source: the federation's own served show documents (promotions/lcw-ltd/)
tenures.note: Co-hosted LTD's own New Blood Rising recap. Returned at Winter's Wrath (11 January 2002) alongside Matt Henstock, was spiked through the announce table by HaVoC during the Presidential match.

caption: LTD's own original announcer, who left with Matt Henstock and returned to call Winter's Wrath from ringside before HaVoC put him through the announce table.

name: Magman

tenures.source: the federation's own served show documents (promotions/lcw-ltd/)
tenures.note: Called the 19 March 2002 Progression show; the federation's own staff page separately credits him as Bob Yobbo Jr.'s long-time former manager, discoverer, and one-time co-owner of an earlier fed.

caption: LTD's own color commentator, a former manager of Bob Yobbo Junior who called the 19 March 2002 Progression show alongside Chad Madden.

name: Dilila Donachello

tenures.source: the federation's own served show documents (promotions/lcw-ltd/)
tenures.note: Billed on LTD's own staff page (capture 26 January 2002) as an interviewer.

caption: LTD's own interviewer, nicknamed "Double D" by Chad Madden on the federation's own staff page.

name: "Sly" Sammy Fox

tenures.source: the federation's own served show documents (promotions/lcw-ltd/)
tenures.note: Billed on LTD's own staff page (capture 26 January 2002) as an interviewer.

caption: LTD's own interviewer, a former independent wrestler and manager turned commentator on the federation's own staff page.

identity.note: Shares the name Sammy Fox with a CCW Cyberspace commentator active in 2005, three years after LTD's own run ends; no document connects the two, and a shared name across unrelated feds is never a merge on its own.

name: Huffman

tenures.source: the federation's own served show documents (promotions/lcw-ltd/)
tenures.note: Lost a Progressive title eliminator to Poltergeist at the 19 March 2002 Progression show. Billed for the LTD Gauntlet at the never-captured Genesis supercard.

caption: Lost a Progressive title eliminator to Poltergeist at the 19 March 2002 Progression show.

identity.note: Shares the name Huffman with an XCWF wrestler; no document connects the two, and a shared name across unrelated feds is never a merge on its own.

name: Jamal "J" Taylor

tenures.source: the federation's own served show documents (promotions/lcw-ltd/)
tenures.note: Lost the opening match of the New Blood Rising tournament (17 November 2001) to Myrddin, having jumped into the ring uninvited after learning he wasn't originally entered.

caption: Stormed the ring uninvited as Myrddin's own mystery opponent at New Blood Rising and lost to a chokeslam inside a minute.
